description: Scan tickets at the gates and doors; admit up to 19,500 people at the Amphitheater in the 90 minutes before a headliner
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Attendee safety: queues longer than about 30 minutes create crowd pressure at the gates; scan manifests are downloaded to scanners before doors, so no data is lost (RPO 0)
manual_workaround: Offline scanning from the manifest downloaded before doors; printed manifests checked by name and order number; wristbands; hold the gates (written procedure exists only at the Amphitheater)
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (manifest and scanning); SYS-09 scanners; SYS-08 Wi-Fi
dependent_people_or_facilities: Door staff and security supervisors; venue General Managers; all three venues
quantified_operational_impact: The Amphitheater must admit about 217 people a minute for 90 minutes; manual checks run at about one third of that rate
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly. Local permit and curfew conditions were not analyzed
attendee_safety_impact: Severe: crowd pressure at gates if queues stall

business_process: Venue safety, security, and crowd management
description: Radios, CCTV and crowd density views, staff door access, and emergency communications on event days
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Doors cannot open without radios and staff door access; CCTV loss is tolerated for one show with extra guards; video older than 24 hours matters only for investigations
manual_workaround: Extra guards at unmonitored areas; manual key control; radio-only coordination; crowd counts by supervisors
dependent_third_parties: Network and security integrator; staffing contractors
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of Safety and Security; venue security supervisors
quantified_operational_impact: 640 cameras and the crowd analytics views at 2 venues go dark; about 60 extra guard hours per Amphitheater show
quantified_regulatory_impact: Venue emergency plans rely on CCTV for egress monitoring
attendee_safety_impact: Severe: egress and crowd density not visible to the command post

description: Card-only sales at 176 fixed points and 108 handhelds across the three venues (cashless venues)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 70% of a show's food and beverage sales fall in the 2 hours around doors and the set break; transactions are held by the POS vendor, so no data is lost
manual_workaround: Offline card acceptance only if the P2PE solution's instruction manual allows it (to be confirmed with the POS vendor); otherwise close stands and bars
dependent_people_or_facilities: Bar and stand staff; event-day workers
quantified_operational_impact: 284 P2PE devices; an Amphitheater show sells about $305,000 of food and beverage
quantified_regulatory_impact: None, unless the offline mode is used outside the P2PE instruction manual (card brand rules)

business_process: Box office window sales and will-call
description: Walk-up sales, will-call, and ticket problem resolution at three box offices on show days
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Box offices open 2 hours before doors; will-call lines must clear before doors; card payments run on standalone P2PE devices
manual_workaround: Will-call from printed lists; direct walk-up buyers to the mobile ticket app
quantified_operational_impact: About 50,000 window sales a year (about 120 per show)
attendee_safety_impact: Moderate: will-call lines near the gates during doors

business_process: Online ticket sales and high-demand on-sales
description: Online sales on website event pages that embed the vendor checkout form, the vendor-hosted fallback pages, and the mobile ticket app, including on-sales with the virtual queue
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A failed on-sale loses demand and can breach artist agreements that set the on-sale time; orders are held by the vendor (vendor RPO 15 minutes, RTO 4 hours meet the targets)
manual_workaround: Reschedule the on-sale with notice to the artist and patrons; send buyers to the vendor-hosted fallback pages if only the website is down
dependent_third_parties: Ticketing vendor; payment partner; cloud provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Vice President of Ticketing; digital team
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,400 online orders on an average day; up to 12,500 tickets in the first hour of a headliner on-sale
quantified_regulatory_impact: Artist agreements fix on-sale times; the FTC fee rule and ADA ticketing rules apply to any rescheduled sale

business_process: Phone, group, and premium seating sales
description: Phone orders, group sales, suite and club seat contracts, and installment charges through the virtual terminal and the card vault
process_owner: Director of Premium Seating and Group Sales
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most phone and premium payments can wait a day; installment charges run from the card vault on fixed dates
manual_workaround: Take orders by callback the next business day; online checkout for group buyers
dependent_systems: SYS-02 virtual terminal and card vault; SYS-11; SYS-07
dependent_people_or_facilities: Premium, group sales, and call center staff
quantified_operational_impact: About 30,000 virtual terminal payments a year (about $60,000 per business day)

description: Settle each show on the night (ticket, food and beverage, and fee splits) and pay artists and promoters
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Artists expect settlement sheets on show night and payment within agreed terms; settlement data can be rebuilt from ticketing and POS reports
manual_workaround: Spreadsheet settlement from ticketing and POS reports; pay the next business day
dependent_systems: SYS-05 settlement application; SYS-01 reports; SYS-03 reports; SYS-13
quantified_operational_impact: About 410 settlements a year; up to 3 on one night
quantified_regulatory_impact: Artist and promoter agreements set settlement terms

description: Lighting, audio, and video for shows; touring crews connect their own equipment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A show stops if audio or lighting fails; consoles run standalone and show files are kept on the consoles and on removable copies
manual_workaround: Consoles run without the network; touring productions usually bring their own
quantified_operational_impact: A stopped Amphitheater show of more than an hour may trigger partial refunds
attendee_safety_impact: Moderate: announcements and video walls carry emergency messages

business_process: Patron communications and urgent event notices
description: Weather holds, cancellations, and schedule changes to ticket holders by email, SMS, app, and website
process_owner: Vice President of Marketing and Digital
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Amphitheater weather holds (for example lightning) must reach up to 19,500 ticket holders within minutes; cancellation notices must go out before doors
manual_workaround: Ticketing platform buyer email and SMS; social media; venue screens and announcements
dependent_people_or_facilities: Marketing and digital team; venue General Managers
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 19,500 recipients per Amphitheater show
attendee_safety_impact: Moderate: attendees may travel to a held or cancelled show

business_process: Website, marketing campaigns, and patron data platform
description: Event calendar and content, email campaigns, audience segments, and the nightly patron copy
process_owner: Vice President of Marketing and Digital
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Campaigns can wait days; if the website is down, buyers use the vendor-hosted fallback pages and the app
manual_workaround: Vendor-hosted event pages; social media; rebuild the patron copy from the ticketing API
dependent_systems: SYS-04; SYS-05 patron data platform; SYS-12
dependent_third_parties: Web agency; marketing agency; cloud provider

description: Patron questions, refunds, and accessible seating requests by phone, email, and the website chatbot
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Accessible seating requests must be handled through the same channels and stages of sale as other sales (28 CFR 36.302(f)(1)(ii)); most other requests can wait a day
manual_workaround: Phone and email queues; chatbot switched off
dependent_people_or_facilities: Guest services and call center staff
quantified_regulatory_impact: ADA Title III ticketing rules for accessible seating requests

description: Venue holds calendar, offers, and performance contracts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Offers and contracts have deadlines of days, not hours
manual_workaround: Email and phone; exported holds calendar

description: Bookkeeping, vendor payments, staffing contractor invoices, and biweekly payroll for 600 employees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; staffing contractors bill weekly; missing payroll has legal and retention impact
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider

description: Rosters, credential badges, and radio assignments for about 1,400 contractor workers and staff on event days
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rosters and badges are prepared the day before a show; the event can run on the prior day's printed roster
manual_workaround: Printed rosters; paper credentials checked at staff doors
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 650 workers at an Amphitheater show
attendee_safety_impact: Moderate: unverified workers in restricted areas

business_process: County PAC ticketing and settlement services (from 2027-07-01)
description: Ticket sales, patron data, and monthly settlement for the County Performing Arts Center under the management agreement
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The agreement requires incident notice within 48 hours, monthly settlement statements, and SOC 2 reports; ticket sales follow BP-05
manual_workaround: Same as BP-04 and BP-05; manual settlement statement from ticketing reports
dependent_people_or_facilities: Ticketing, finance, and County PAC staff
quantified_regulatory_impact: County agreement terms (contract), including SOC 2 commitments
